source.title: The Dynamic of Consensus in Deep Networks and the Identification of Noisy Labels
source.authors: Daniel Shwartz; Uri Stern; Daphna Weinshall

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures test-accuracy changes over training in deep-network ensembles under label noise, but it does not use a double-descent sweep or report the full claimed curve.
record.gate_note: The paper studies overfitting and agreement dynamics, not double descent. Its own relevant result is a qualitative report that test accuracy drops when overfit occurs during training with label noise. It cites Deep Double Descent as background but does not test model size, sample size, or a complete fall-rise-fall trajectory over epochs. Noise-identification, filtration, and classifier-accuracy results do not measure the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The paper studies inter-network agreement and noisy-label filtration (DisagreeNet). It cites Deep Double Descent only as background on bias and variance falling with complexity. It runs no sweep of model size, sample size or regularization. Its only epoch-wise result is a qualitative statement that test accuracy drops when overfit occurs under label noise (Sec. 3.3, Fig. 2b). That shows a single rise in test error, with no reported second descent, so it cannot bear on whether an epoch-wise fall-rise-fall curve exists. The fall-then-rise the paper does describe (Sec. 3.2, Fig. 2a) is in the agreement Bimodality Index, not in test error.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right. The main conclusion is that prediction variability across an ensemble of deep networks is much larger on noisy labels than on clean ones. The ensemble-agreement score (ELP) built on this, DisagreeNet, beats baselines in noise-level estimation, noise filtration and supervised classification without a clean validation set or a known noise level. The overfit-agreement link is a supporting observation, not the headline.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines overfitting and inter-network agreement in noisy-label training rather than sweeping model size, training duration for a double-descent curve, or sample size.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors state that the agreement-drop prediction is observed when overfit occurs and is not observed when overfit does not occur.

fits_no_version.finding: With label noise, when overfit occurs, a test-accuracy drop co-occurs with a drop in the ensemble agreement index BI. In linear regression trained with gradient descent, the authors prove overfit implies decreasing inter-model agreement.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Overfitting during training on noisy labels coincides with falling inter-network prediction agreement in deep ensembles.

record.problems: The relevant evidence is qualitative; the text gives no numerical epoch-wise test-error series for the reported drop, and does not establish the full curve.
record.rows_left_out: Other results concern noisy-label detection, filtration, and classification performance rather than the claim versions; cited double-descent findings are not this study's results.

untested.parts: No epoch-wise test-error curve showing a second descent is reported.

record.verdict_notes: No verdicts are given: the study does not test any version. The single row is a qualitative overfit statement unrelated to a double-descent sweep.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size sweep or interpolation-threshold test.
The paper reports a test-accuracy drop during overfitting, but does not establish the full fall-rise-fall curve or a second descent over training epochs.
No training-sample-size sweep near an interpolation threshold.

rows.check: The text says only that test accuracy drops when overfit occurs, shown in Fig. 2b as test accuracy plotted against train bimodality, not against epochs. The later 'fall and rise' in Sec. 3.2 concerns the agreement index BI, not test error.
